R335.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/get_result correctly parameterizes username; identical return shape and error handling.

R336.note: Removes the stray opt-out so the app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute applies; comment confirms the legacy exemption is stale, no legitimate caller is affected.

R337.note: Captures node->next before free(); standard safe traversal, preserves refresh_session calls and continuation for live nodes.

R338.note: CGI::escapeHTML() (importable as a plain function via `use CGI qw(escapeHTML)`) correctly neutralizes <, >, &, " in the injected values with no other behavior change.

R339.note: Replaces string-evaluated assert() with a direct boolean check that throws on failure, matching the original assert-on-failure semantics without the code-injection sink.

R340.note: Argument array + shell=False closes the injection; alphanumeric-only regex validation matches the docstring's own stated contract for report_id, so no legitimate value is rejected.

R341.note: Switching to IMemcachedClient.Store() is an appropriate sink fix, but it swaps the constructor's dependency type (Socket -> IMemcachedClient) and adds a new library dependency, a disclosed but breaking change for any existing caller/DI wiring; explanation also mislabels the memcached wire format as 'RESP', which is Redis's protocol, not memcached's.

R342.note: Allowlists field before interpolation while term/tenant_id stay bound; default 'name' still permitted, matches the stated contract.

R343.note: Narrow DTO + server-set IsAdmin is the correct format-preserving fix, but it also silently forces Balance to always 0 on import (disclosed only via a code comment 'or fetch from database'), removing any legitimate ability to set an initial balance.

R344.note: Allowlist check runs before require() and keeps 'summary' as an allowed/default value, matching the stated contract.

R345.note: Wrapping ruleSource in "(function(){ return ("+ruleSource+"); })" does not sandbox anything -- the attacker fully controls the text and can close the parens/braces early and append arbitrary statements (e.g. Java.type(...).getRuntime().exec(...)) that execute during the eval() call itself, so the code-injection vector is not actually closed.

R346.note: Standard parameterized query with cursor.execute(query, (customer_id,)); behavior otherwise identical.

R347.note: Adds Authentication param and calls the existing findByOwnerUsername(), mirroring the sibling detail endpoint exactly as the contract requires.

R348.note: isOwnedBy() is hardcoded to `return false`, so after this fix no owner -- including legitimate ones -- can ever delete their own document, contradicting 'authorized owners can still delete... and receive 204'; also throws AccessDeniedException (403), which reveals more than the contract's required not-found-equivalent denial path, and neither issue is called out as a required follow-up in the explanation.

R349.note: Wraps the route with the existing requireAdmin middleware exactly like its sibling routes; no other change.

R350.note: Allowlist maps recognized command verbs to fixed handler names before call_user_func_array(), the canonical fix for user-controlled callables; new handler names are openly introduced as part of the allowlist design.

R351.note: build_resp_command() correctly emits length-prefixed RESP bulk strings (Redis's real wire protocol), making embedded CRLF in key or locale unable to act as a delimiter; response handling unchanged.

R352.note: Fixes the call target to a single named procedure with the attacker value bound via setString(), the only sound remedy since a procedure identifier cannot itself be parameterized; the behavior change (fixed procedure name) is stated plainly and is required by the fix.

R353.note: Positional '?' placeholder with OdbcCommand.Parameters.Add binds searchTerm as data; wildcard formatting and result handling unchanged.
